source.title: Irish News, 3 June 1939, p. 6 ("Downpatrick rural election: seat won back for Nationalists")
source.publisher: Irish News (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Votes from the Irish News (3 June 1939, p. 6) and Belfast News-Letter (3 June 1939, p. 3).

note: Triennial election of the Downpatrick Rural District Council, polled at the end of May 1939. The two contested divisions, Ardglass and Downpatrick Rural, were counted on 2 June; Castlewellan Urban had three nominations, but two withdrew and Felix M'Kenna was returned unopposed (Belfast News-Letter, 11 May 1939, p. 5). Filed on 1939-06-01, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Down that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1939-05-31 (verification 5 Nov 2026). Killinchy and Raholp are recorded from the report of the new council's annual meeting of 7 June 1939, with their divisions from the 1930 return (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). Dignam was printed 'Jignam' in the Irish News and 'Dignum' in the News-Letter.
